object_types.name: Customer
object_types.definition: A party that places orders in the system. Identified by a unique customer ID in the CRM.

source_references.excerpt: A customer places an order. Every order belongs to exactly one customer, and customers can place multiple orders over time.
Each customer has a unique customer ID in the CRM system.

One more thing -- I've heard some people call customers "clients" in the billing system. Are those the same thing? Good question. In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: Client vs. Customer terminology: The transcript indicates that the CRM system uses 'Customer' but the billing team calls them 'Clients,' with a note that the billing team 'only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.' This suggests a potential difference in scope: should the model distinguish between customers (anyone who places an order) vs. clients (customers who have completed payment)? Or are they genuinely the same entity with no business rule distinction? If they are distinct, we would need to model when a customer becomes a client (e.g., via a paid invoice), and constraints on which entity places orders vs. completes payments.
